LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about chores and fun activities.
•	 To understand obligation, lack of obligation and advice.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#5 Days of the Week Song
•	 TR#9 Prepositions Action Song
•	 TR#10 Puppy Song 
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home 
•	 Moods A5 flash cards 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 8: Days of the Week cards 
(P.1.5)

•	 Teacher materials for Act. 3: Character and Fun Activities 
cards (P.1.2) and Fun Activity/Chores memory cards 
(P.1.1)

2.– ACTIVITY 8: DAYS OF THE WEEK SONG (TR#5) (5’)
P.1.5
Monday
> Warm-Up
To begin with, take the days of the week flash cards from Act. 
5 (P.1.5). Ask, “What’s the first day of the week?”. Encourage 
Ss to say, “It’s Monday.”
Then place the Monday flash card up on the whiteboard and 
ask, “What comes after Monday?”, to which Ss should answer 
“After Monday comes Tuesday.”. If the Ss aren’t sure, show 
them the flash cards and ask: “Is it Friday? Is it Wednesday?” 
etc. Continue until you’ve placed all the Day cards on the board 
in order. 
> Main Activity
Sing and dance to the song following the instructions written 
in brackets.
DAYS OF THE WEEK SONG
(Ss sitting on the floor and whispering)
Monday, Tuesday
Here we come,
Wednesday, Thursday,
Let’s get it done! (Ss fist-pump the air)
Friday is here,
We’re ready to cheer! (Ss stand up)
Here comes the weekend,

Hip hip hurray! (Ss cheer)
Saturday, Sunday,
They are both cool days! (Ss dance)
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday,
Saturday aaand Sunday! (repeat) 
(pointing to the different days of the week cards on the 
board)
NOTE: for the last part of the choreography, you can also 
give each S a day card and have them show it when the day 
is mentioned in the last two verses.
3.– STORY WITH CHANGES (PP.8-16) (9’)
Tell the Ss the second half of the story using the variables 
from last week. Please see the section on storytelling in the 
Warm-Up Routines Index. 
4.– WORKSHEET: MY CHORES (P.7) (9’)
My Chores
I have to...
I don’t have to...
7

MATERIALS
•	 P&P SB1 Page 7 Stickers 
NOTE: if you collected your Ss’ books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying, “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted. 
In this worksheet, Ss must place stickers on each column 
according to what they have to or don’t have to do at home. 
Go over the different chores on the stickers by saying what 
your chores are. For example, pointing to the corresponding 
stickers, say, “I have to make the bed every day and I don’t 
have sweep the floor.” Next, ask each S, “What do you have to 
do at home?”. They should say for example, “I have to...every 
day. I don’t have to…”

To finish, you can ask them to make a phrase about their 
classmate on their right, for example, “She has to feed the 
dog every day and she doesn’t have to take out the rubbish.”
NOTE: if there is a chore that is not shown on the stickers, 
they can use the pencils to draw a simple picture to represent 
it, but they should not spend much time drawing it. Tell them 
they have just two minutes to do this.

6.–ACTIVITY 1: MY CHORES (9’)
P.1.1
P.1.1
P.1.1
TARGET LANGUAGE FOR FUN ACTIVITIES
Play video games
Read a book
Listen to music
Talk on the phone
Watch TV
Draw a picture
Ride my bike
Play football
Roller-skate
Play in the park

TARGET LANGUAGE FOR CHORES
Wash Billy
Feed Billy
Take Billy for a walk
Brush Billy
Give Billy some water
Pick up Billy’s poo
Lay the table
Make the bed
Take out the rubbish
Sweep the floor
Clear the table 
> How to Play
Ss must find the activities that match those on their bingo 
board. In order to win, the Ss must find all their chores first, 
and then their fun activity. 
> Warm-Up
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
Start by drilling the target language. Spread the Chores cards 
(P.1.1) on the table and say: “Wow! Look at my chores. I have 
a lot of things to do! I have to feed Billy (signal to the Ss to 
repeat after you), wash Billy, etc.” 
Now review the fun activities. Start by saying: “This is what I 
want to do. I want to...”. Show the Ss the Fun Activity cards one 
by one and let them finish the sentence with the fun activity. 
> Main Activity
Hand out an A5 Bingo board (P.1.1) to each S. Then spread 
out the Memory cards, which show the chores and fun activities 
(P.1.1), face down on the table.
Choose a S to go first. You can check out the different tips on 
how to start a game at the beginning of this guide. The S turns 
over a Memory card and identifies the activity by saying one of 
the following phrases depending on the scenario: 
•	 If they have it: “I have to...” 
•	 If they don’t have it: “I don’t have to...” 
•	 If they find a fun activity before their chores: “I can’t ... 
now, I must ... first.” For instance: “I can’t play video 
games now, I must wash the puppy, clear the table 
and make the bed first.” 
The first S to collect all their chores followed by their fun 
activity is the winner.
> Follow-Up
Once you have finished the activity, point to the winner’s 
board and ask the Ss, “What chores must Jane do first?” to

which they should reply “Jane must clear the table, take out 
the rubbish and make the bed first and THEN she can listen 
to music.”
7.– ACTIVITY 3: GUESSING GAME (7’)
P.1.1
P.1.2
P.1.2
> Warm-Up
Place a character card (P.1.2) on the table and shuffle the Fun 
Activity cards (P.1.2). One at a time, place the Fun Activity cards 
(P.1.1) next to the character and ask the Ss: “What is Grandpa/
Pam/etc. doing?”. Encourage them to respond by saying “He/
she’s listening to music.”
> Main Activity
Place one of each of the Fun Activity cards (P.1.1 - without 
the chores) face up on the table so the Ss can use them as a 
visual reference. Then put the Character cards (P.1.2) next to 
the Fun Activity cards from Act. 2 (P.1.2) on the table face down. 
Model the activity for the Ss. First, take a Character card (P.1.2) 
and place it face up on the table. Then take a Fun Activity card 
(P.1.2) but don’t show it to the Ss. They must guess what the 
character is doing by asking you questions.
So, for example, if you take a Mum card, they should ask, 
“What is Mum doing?” and then gesture to the Fun Activity 
cards (P.1.1) that are face up on the table. The Ss must use 
these cards as a reference to make a guess. The Ss must take 
it in turns to ask, “Is she watching TV?” to which you should 
answer, “No, she isn’t.” or “Yes, she’s watching TV.”
When a S guesses correctly, it’s their turn to take a Character 
card and a new Fun Activity card and repeat the steps above. 
Make sure every S participates at least once.
> Follow-Up
Take a Character card and a Fun Activity card. Ask wrong 
questions on purpose by saying actions that aren’t depicted 
on your card, for example, “Is Dad playing in the park?” to

which Ss should answer, “No, he isn’t playing in the park. He 
is watching TV.” 
8.– ACTIVITY 7: SWITCH (5’)
> How to Play
This is a group hand clapping game to practise counting. To 
play, you must have all the Ss sitting in a circle, either on the 
floor or at the table.
> Main Activity
If you do the activity sitting on chairs, the Ss should sit with 
their palms facing up on the table. If you do it on the floor, the 
Ss place their palms on their legs.
The Ss must place their right hand on top of the hand of the 
S sitting to their right, and their left hand underneath the hand 
of the person on their left. This way when they begin to clap, 
they will use their right hand to clap the hand of the person 
to their left and the clapping will continue around the circle. 
Start counting from number 50 until you get to 99. If someone 
makes a mistake, the Ss switch the position of their hands (right 
hand below, left hand on top). If this is too difficult, simply move 
on with the game without switching hand positions. 
NOTE: if time allows, increase the difficulty by starting from 
number one or counting backwards.

10.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.
BONUS
ACTIVITY 9: PREPOSITIONS (TR#9)
> Warm-Up
The Ss should perform the following actions to rehearse 
the movements.
•	 March in line. (all the Ss march in a single file line)
•	 Hide under the table.
•	 Walk next to a friend.
•	 Stand between two chairs.
•	 Jump behind the teacher. (all the Ss jump on the spot 
behind the teacher)
•	 Run in front of the (white) board. (all the Ss run on 
the spot in front of the board)
•	 Sit on a chair.
> Main Activity
Then play the Prepositions Actions Song (TR#9) and dance 
to it.
PREPOSITIONS ACTIONS SONG
(as you sing, simply perform the actions mentioned in the song. 
You can also create a hand choreography for the preposition 
verses.) 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
March in line, in, in line. 
(musical interlude)
Hide under the table, under, under the table.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Walk next to a friend, next to, next to a friend. 
(musical interlude)
Stand between two chairs, between, between two chairs.

In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Jump behind the teacher, behind, behind the teacher. 
(musical interlude)
Run in front of the board, in front of, in front of the board.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Sit on a chair, on, on a chair. 
(musical interlude)
This is the end, the end, the end.
ACTIVITY 4: CHARADES (VERSION 1) 
P.1.2
> Warm-Up
Quickly drill the Fun Activities (P.1.2.). Show the cards one by 
one and point to one of your Ss saying the action, for example 
“Jane is watching TV.”. In this case, Jane will have to mime 
watching TV.
> Main Activity
A S takes a card showing one fun activity (P.1.2.). They must 
mime the action and ask, “What am I doing?”. The others must 
guess by asking, “Are you watching TV?” and the S miming 
must respond either, “No, I’m not.” or “Yes, I am.”. Do as many 
rounds as time allows.
